groups.takeaway: The 12-frame noiseless tutorial loop reduces the final-half residual from 148.6 to 84.4 nm (fraction 0.568). TSVD reaches its 8.58 nm minimum command error once 29 modes are kept. Delay limits usable gain: with two frames of latency the RMS ratio rises from 0.723 at gain 0.2 to 1.746 at gain 1.0, i.e. the loop amplifies the disturbance. More actuators help at 1.5 m (246.7 -> 227.5 nm from 5 to 9 across).

context.science_residual_of_these_records: @3 review scan and camera comparison: pre-update. They name 663df161 with a source-change digest equal to that of the 663df161 -> 573f875 diff of src and scripts (no untracked files), so they ran on the code of commit 573f875, whose science_run builds the accumulator without a residual argument and so uses the default pre-update residual. @1 and @2 scans: unknown (their records carry no code identity).

The 12 m record ran on the code of commit 573f875, which computes this estimator. charts.transformation: seed means dv_mean_nm2 (= seed mean of each run's noise_variance_m2 x 1e18, checked against the isolation records) and their SEs exactly as saved by the saved-data reanalysis; no fit line is drawn

groups.takeaway: For background and plain pixel processing the camera model's centroid noise agrees with Monte-Carlo to within 2.4 % at every supported flux point; the negative_clipped and thresholded variants have no point inside the model's domain. Open-loop slope-noise propagation agrees with prediction (mean measured/predicted variance 0.996-1.004). At 12 m the faint end is set by measurement validity and reconstruction policy: the @3 review rerun reaches 195.2 nm and Strehl 0.708 at m_AB 11, while at m_AB 12 no measurement is valid and the residual equals open loop, even though the lost_lock_runs field reads 0. The predeclared inverse-photon test fails at 12 m (slope -1.0282 +/- 0.0105, chi2/dof 2.50) and passes at 2 m (-0.9782 +/- 0.0136); the 6.7 % dip at m_AB 10 and the 2 m drift remain unexplained.
limitations: Profile revisions @1, @2 and @3 differ in control policy and are post-hoc revisions; their rows are not one experiment.
lost_lock only compares the final post-update residual with the final open-loop residual; it is not a lock classifier, and a run with zero valid measurements reads as not lost.
The noise-law verdict depends on using the unscaled fit errors (scaled errors would pass at 12 m); the test was predeclared with unscaled errors. S4 and LIM-18 are not closed.
Synthetic engineering camera presets without datasheets; this is not measured instrument performance.
evidence_notes: dV is not a difference of variances: for 2 m m_AB 5 (seeds 61-68) the plotted dV is 4.2700 nm^2, while the seed mean of the arms' mean-square difference (mean_square_difference_m2) is -38.5574 nm^2. The latter is not plotted.

The 12 m isolation record has the source identity of commit 573f875 (its digest equals the 663df161 -> 573f875 diff), whose paired_noise_run computes noise_variance_m2 as defined here. The 2 m record names 663df161 with uncommitted changes that match no commit; its estimator is the one the saved-data reanalysis documents (report.md, section 2) and later committed as detector_level._paired_noise_core. The reanalysis re-derives the record's quoted aggregates but cannot recompute dV (no residual maps were saved), so the 2 m estimator is documented, not reproduced.

The paired-noise fits are not stored in the run records (their summary is empty); they are read from the saved-data reanalysis docs/research/detector_noise_law/results.json, whose recorded script path predates its rename.
The README's 279 nm CMOS figure is a rounding of an earlier (non-review) record's 278.46 nm; the reviewed value is shown here.
E3/E4 records carry no profile-id field; the revision comes from each record's command and the status document.

groups.takeaway: In this analytical MCAO adapter the completed on-axis residual is 131.7 nm, peak Strehl 0.781 and energy within a 50 mas radius 0.635 at 1.65 um. Completing the fitting tail matters: fitting grows from 47.9 nm on the original grid to 71.3 nm. Across the recorded seeing scan the 50 mas energy falls 27.1 % while the sampled core width changes by only 0.26 mas; that is a differential change at fixed 5 mas sampling, comparable to the 0.50 % (0.22 mas) bias of the width estimator, not an absolute width.
limitations: A separate analytical study: not a time-domain LGS/MCAO extension of the native SCAO loop and not an unmodified TIPTOP prediction.
Its wavelength, residual convention, profile and budget are not comparable to the native SCAO results in R1-R5 or the 2 m experiment.
Original producer and date fields are absent from the record; a current notebook hash does not establish current-code execution.
Energy is within a 50 mas radius (not diameter), with the full-field flux as denominator.

FWHM values are sampled-contour estimates with a -0.50 % (5 mas pixels) / -0.12 % (2.5 mas) bias against the analytic annular reference; the seeing-scan width change is differential and must not be quoted as an absolute width.
evidence_notes: The five figures were written by fig.savefig at 150 dpi and are not byte-identical to the notebook's 120 dpi inline outputs; they are bound by file hash.
The 27.1 % energy drop is computed here from $.seeing_records[0] and [-1]; it is not a stored scalar.
The notebook attributes the configuration to P3's MavisMCAO.ini, the README to TIPTOP's; the source is ambiguous.
No TIPTOP, P3 or MASTSEL licence text is recorded in the repository; versions are pinned (astro-tiptop 1.5.1, astro-p3 1.6.2, mastsel 1.5.2).
